title: Review of lab 1's xcell-evo2-S: Supported for I and D (both fresh seeds reach generation 3 with 0 merges). B is by construction: the membrane m is a band-pass readout 4s(1-s) of the body
summary: labkit re-runs of the lab 1 world (unchanged) on fresh seeds 11 and 12 (T=2000, 128^2): from 10 planted bodies, 9 and 5 persistent splits, max generation 3 on both, 0 merges. The bodies stay round and similar in size, with a closed m rim, which labkit flags as membrane-like on every top track (rim/core and rim/outside >= 1.5). This is better than lab 1's 2 of 6 runs at generation 3 or more. Reading world.py: m's drive is W*gfun('band', Z_u) = 2*4s(1-s) with s = tanh(Z_u/0.6) of the body field, plus a Cahn-Hilliard term on m. That is RUBRIC L3's 'band-pass readout of the body', so the rim is a contour by construction. Whether it does work rests on lab 1's r3 gate ablation, which I did not re-run (m gates c, q and h through perm terms). Deaths are imposed disk erasures (KILL_RATE 0.1), and division is the Gray-Scott-class splitting of the u body.
